Subject: Redwood benchmark follow-up: Latency & throughput next steps (Globex)

Hi Matt —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: validate p95/p99 latency and sustained tokens/sec for your customer-facing chat endpoints; compare Redwood Dedicated vs your current hyperscaler endpoint under realistic traffic shapes.
- What we heard: ~60 RPS steady-state with 200-400 token responses, 95th latency target ~120ms, hard p99 requirement <300ms for peak load.
- Proposed technical next steps: 1) Jonas runs a short A/B benchmark (Redwood vs hyperscaler) with your 3 canonical prompts and our recommended batching/quantization; 2) share raw p95/p99 and tokens/sec, plus configuration JSON; 3) iterate on batching and KV cache warm-up to optimize p99.

Attachments: I attached the Redwood vs Hyperscaler Q1 benchmark summary and a starter AB-test plan CSV. Jonas will own the run; Dev will join if we need to adjust runtime params.

Can you confirm: 1) which region you want tests run from (us-west/us-east/eu)? 2) a 1-hour window when your infra team can allow the traffic?

If that works, Jonas and I will schedule the test and share an off-the-record quick checklist for the run.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Attachment: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_q1_benchmarks.pdf (summary PDF, ~6 pages)

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments. Quick answers: we want tests from us-east (primary region). Our infra team can give you a 90-min window next Thursday (Feb 18) from 09:00–10:30 ET. That should be enough to run a couple of sustained scenarios and ramp tests.

A few clarifying questions before you run anything: 
1) For p99: can you run both cold-start and warmed-cache scenarios? We care about user experience for both.
2) Can you also include a tokens/sec breakdown per model variant (4-bit quant vs fp16) — we may be sensitive to quality regressions.

I'll loop Sara (platform lead) on scheduling and she'll share the infra contact for firewall whitelisting.

—Matt

Matt / Sara —

Great, thanks for the window. Jonas and I sketched the test plan; attaching the AB-test CSV you can drop into your infra team's load harness. High-level notes on what we'll measure: 

- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) for each model/config under steady-state and ramp phases
- sustained tokens/sec (aggregate and per-connection)
- error rate / timeouts per 1k requests
- cold start (empty KV cache) vs warmed (5k prefix warmup)

Jonas: can you run the initial Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler A/B (same prompt set) from us-east on Feb 18 at 09:15 ET? Please use: 
- Redwood configs: default batching, batching window 8ms, dynamic kv cache enabled, quantization profile Q4_{balanced}
- Hyperscaler: standard endpoint; try to match concurrency and payload sizes.

We'll upload the raw CSV and a summary PDF post-run. If p99 is >300ms we will try batching/window changes and a smaller model variant.

Thanks —
Marissa

Matt/Sara/Marissa —

Confirming test slot on Feb 18 at 09:15 ET. Quick technical notes so infra has what they need: 

- IPs to whitelist (Redwood Dedicated egress): 54.210.23.11, 54.210.23.12
- API keys: I'll generate a scoped test key valid for 6 hours and share to Sara over the secure channel.
- Test plan: 3 prompts x 2 model configs x 2 cache states (cold/warmed) x ramp (0→150 RPS) → steady 60 RPS for 20 minutes → burst to 200 RPS for 5 minutes.

Preliminary acceptance criteria (for the AB run):
- p95 < 150ms, p99 < 300ms for steady-state; errors < 0.5%
- tokens/sec reported per-minute and aggregated across the test window

I'll produce a results CSV and a short PDF summary within 4 hours of test completion. If the hyperscaler shows lower p99 but higher cost per token, we'll highlight tradeoffs (latency vs unit cost).

-Jonas
